status: Implemented; iPhone and iPad simulator regressions passed; unsigned device build passed
issue: Cat Catch's Open download directory button did nothing.

root_cause.publisher_handler: The unmodified Microsoft Store package's js/downloader.js and js/m3u8.js call chrome.downloads.show(downloadId), or chrome.downloads.showDefaultFolder() when there is no ID.
root_cause.missing_bridge: The compatibility layer already exposed chrome.downloads, but omitted both folder methods. Cat Catch's polyfill only supplies its fallback when the entire downloads object is absent.

implementation.scope: Generic extension compatibility layer; no Cat Catch publisher HTML, CSS or JavaScript modified.
implementation.showDefaultFolder: Present the existing native LibraryFilesView at the app's Documents/Downloads directory.
implementation.show: Validate the extension-owned download ID and open the downloaded file's containing directory. This implementation does not select or scroll to an individual file.
implementation.javascript_signature: Both methods return undefined, matching the Chrome void signatures. Invalid numeric IDs throw TypeError; asynchronous native failures are logged.
implementation.permissions: Existing downloads permission gate remains active. Foreign or unknown download IDs cannot reveal files through show().
implementation.lifecycle: Present the native file browser above the extension document, with a Done button. Closing it retains the source popup/page and JavaScript state. Repeated folder requests reuse the existing host.
implementation.existing_installations: The native extension context loader refreshes its private compatibility script on load; reimporting the extension is not required.

generic_download_test: Real Blob and data downloads retain expected byte counts and SHA-256 hashes, including an empty file and a Blob larger than 32 MiB.
Both folder APIs return undefined and present the actual native file browser.
Repeated calls reuse the folder controller; dismissing preserves the source document sentinel.
A second extension cannot reveal another extension's download ID; the native failure reaches runtime.lastError.
real_cat_catch_test: Used the unmodified Microsoft Store Cat Catch 2.7.4 package.
Called showDefaultFolder inside the actual publisher popup; verified native presentation and retained popup state after dismissal.
After a real cookie-bearing download completed, searched for its extension download ID and called show(id) inside the publisher popup; verified native presentation.
Existing popup localization, footer layout, media capture, completion events, playable preview, media controls and supplied Bilibili page checks passed.
validation.permission_regression: Existing undeclared-permissions native compatibility test passed on iPhone.

visual_review.result: Reviewed both screenshots: the native file list and Done action are visible with usable sheet layouts on iPhone and iPad.

validation.localization: Strict check passed: 881 Localizable, 500 ReadingTools and 81 FeatureImprovements keys across 50 locales.
validation.metadata: Generated JSON check passed for 50 locales; version and store content unchanged.

fixture_cleanup.iphone: Restored the pre-existing QA package from the byte-for-byte backup in the current app container.
fixture_cleanup.ipad: Removed only the newly staged QA package after verifying its hash in the current app container.
fixture_cleanup.download_files: Tests remove only their newly created downloads. Pre-existing files and extension installations are preserved.

limits: No physical-device execution; the device target compiled unsigned.
The real publisher popup tests invoke the folder APIs directly. The downloader.html Open directory handler was source-inspected, not clicked in an end-to-end UI test.
These tests cover the named APIs and regressions; they do not certify every Chrome extension feature.
